title: Nova
desc: Rebuilding a fintech dashboard around trust and speed.
overview: Nova's dashboard had grown one feature at a time for three years, and it showed. Every number competed for the same attention, so nothing actually got read. The brief was to rebuild the core dashboard around a single question: what does this person need to decide right now?
approach: We cut the dashboard's default view from eleven modules to three, and let people opt back in to the rest. Motion carries the hierarchy — the primary number settles first, everything secondary arrives a beat later and quieter.
Every state — loading, empty, error — was designed as its own screen, not a spinner bolted onto the happy path.
outcome: Time-to-first-decision dropped by 40% in testing, and support tickets tagged "confusing dashboard" fell by more than half in the first quarter after launch.

title: Drift
desc: An identity system for a slow-travel platform.
overview: Drift books slow, unhurried trips — trains instead of flights, weeks instead of long weekends. The identity needed to feel like the opposite of a booking app: patient, tactile, a little analog.
approach: The wordmark is set slightly loose, like it hasn't decided to arrive yet. A single custom grain texture appears everywhere — on the site, on printed tickets, in the app splash — as a consistent tactile signature.
Color shifts by season rather than staying fixed, so the brand itself feels like it's moving through a year.
outcome: Drift's rebrand shipped alongside a 22% lift in newsletter-to-booking conversion, and the grain motif has since been picked up by three of their regional partners.

title: Fieldnote
desc: A journaling app that writes back.
overview: Fieldnote is a journaling app that occasionally writes back — short, gentle prompts generated from your own past entries. The design challenge was making that feel considerate, not surveillant.
approach: Every prompt is visually distinct from the user's own writing — different weight, different color, always dismissible in one tap. Nothing appears without an obvious, low-friction way to close it.
We built a full motion spec for "arriving" content so nothing ever just pops in — it settles, the way a thought does.
outcome: Daily active writing sessions grew 31% after launch, and qualitative interviews showed the prompts were consistently described as "thoughtful" rather than "creepy" — the bar we'd set internally.

title: Echo Room
desc: Spatial audio brand for a live-music startup.
overview: Echo Room streams spatial-audio live sets. The identity needed to suggest sound moving through space without leaning on any of the genre's usual waveform clichés.
approach: Instead of waveforms, the mark is built from concentric rings that distort based on the loudness of whatever's actually playing — a real, live piece of the brand rather than a static logo.
Typography stays completely still by contrast, so the one moving element always reads as intentional.
outcome: The live mark became the most-screenshotted brand asset across the platform's first season, according to Echo Room's own social monitoring.

title: Kinetic Type
overview: An open-source playground for pairing variable fonts with real physics — type that responds to gravity, cursor velocity, and scroll, instead of pre-baked keyframes.
approach: Every letterform's weight and width axis is tied to a small physics simulation rather than a timeline, so no two sessions ever animate quite the same way.
Released as a small open-source library so other designers could drop the same behavior into their own type.
outcome: Crossed 4,000 GitHub stars in its first year and became the starting point for the kinetic headline used across this site.
